page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-64GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a split profile. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is positioned in the bottom 10%, while multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall within the middle 50% average. Memory performance shows a similar divergence; cached small-block read bandwidth is average, but uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Passmark memory scores are also weak. For specialized workloads, the server achieves average results in Redis SET operations and small-model LLM inference, but drops to poor performance for larger 7B model text generation. Static web serving throughput is also weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 on a shared CPU infrastructure, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance single-core execution. The lack of bundled local storage means storage resources must be provisioned externally. This configuration is best suited for memory-heavy but CPU-tolerant workloads such as caching layers, medium-sized database operations, and general-purpose memory-optimized tasks.
